beats.line: Flip a coin. That's your odds of your state legislative race actually being contested in Massachusetts.
beats.prompt: A single silver coin spinning mid-air above a worn wooden table in a dimly lit room, dramatic side lighting casting a long shadow, mood tense and uncertain.

beats.line: Since 2014, 51% of races in this state — more than half — have had just ONE name on the ballot. No opponent. No debate. No choice.
beats.prompt: A stark white paper ballot on a plain gray surface with a single printed line and one checkbox, harsh overhead fluorescent light, mood clinical and hollow.

beats.line: Massachusetts ranks dead last in the country for electoral competitiveness.
beats.prompt: A printed list or ranked chart pinned to a corkboard with the bottom entry circled in red ink, natural window light from the side, mood bleak and bureaucratic.

beats.line: And it's not because good candidates don't exist — it's because the system makes it nearly impossible for a challenger to even get on the ballot in the first place.
beats.prompt: A heavy closed wooden door with a large iron padlock in a stark institutional hallway, cool blue ambient light, mood forbidding and exclusionary.

beats.line: Voters show up… to rubber-stamp a decision that was already made for them.
beats.prompt: A red rubber stamp pressing down onto a white document on a government office desk, motion blur on the stamp, warm incandescent light, mood resigned and mechanical.
